mechanisms.label: Military energy autonomy
mechanisms.summary: Recent U.S. military procurement actions demonstrate a shift toward deployable autonomous power at bases, indicating progress from pilot projects toward broader deployment of microreactor technology.

observed_evidence.claim: The Department of the Air Force, together with the Defense Innovation Unit, selected three companies to potentially develop and operate a microreactor on a DAF installation as part of the Advanced Nuclear Power for Installations initiative, with Buckley Space Force Base, Colorado, and Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana, identified as the first two sites.
observed_evidence.why_upstream: This procurement step moves the Air Force from concept to concrete development contracts for on‑base microreactors, a key step toward autonomous base power.
observed_evidence.source_name: DAF announces next steps in Advanced Nuclear Power for Installations initiative  > Air Force > Article Display

observed_evidence.claim: The Department of Defense broke ground on the Project Pele transportable microreactor project at Idaho National Laboratory, a demonstration that could become one of the first advanced reactors to operate in the United States as early as 2026.
observed_evidence.why_upstream: Ground‑breaking a transportable microreactor prototype signals the DoD’s intent to field deployable, autonomous power sources for forward operating bases.
observed_evidence.source_name: Department of Defense Breaks Ground on Project Pele Microreactor | Department of Energy

observed_evidence.claim: The U.S. Army tapped five firms to build on‑base nuclear microreactors, investing billions of dollars, with Antares Nuclear slated to develop a microreactor at Fort Bragg, North Carolina.
observed_evidence.why_upstream: Awarding contracts to multiple vendors for on‑site reactors demonstrates a transition from experimental pilots to operational deployment.
observed_evidence.source_name: US Army taps 5 firms to build on-base microreactors in nuclear energy push

observed_evidence.claim: The U.S. Army announced plans to build nuclear microreactors on five military bases as part of the Janus Program, selecting five vendors and assigning each to a different installation.
observed_evidence.why_upstream: Deploying microreactors on multiple Army installations expands autonomous power capability beyond pilot testing.
observed_evidence.source_name: The US Army is betting on nuclear microreactors to keep its bases powered even if the grid goes dark
